effort: Produce independent arm force while keeping the trunk facing forward.

explosive.name: Medicine Ball Two-Hand Receive to Single-Arm Forward Return
explosive.job: Primary transfer from a symmetric received load to an independent arm release while staying square.
explosive.cue: Coach gives a gentle chest-height feed; receive with both hands, settle briefly at the selected shoulder, remove assisting hand and push forward. Complete one arm's reps then change sides; no rotational wind-up.
explosive.replacement: a self-started stationary single-arm shot-put throw when receiving quality or ball control is unconfirmed; use a secured single-arm band press if release setup fails
explosive.uniqueness_reason: First bilateral load acceptance into unilateral release. This coordination task differs from bilateral catch-return and self-start single-arm throws; immediate one-hand catches were rejected.
explosive.key: Medicine Ball Two-Hand Receive to Single-Arm Forward Return

explosive.name: One-Arm Row — supported dumbbell speed pull
explosive.job: Express the backward draw independently without opposite-arm assistance.
explosive.cue: Hand and knee supported on inspected bench; light dumbbell, quick elbow-to-hip pull, lower 2 s, still reset; no torso rotation.
explosive.replacement: a thigh-supported light dumbbell row with the same side dose if bench fit is unsuitable
explosive.uniqueness_reason: First rapid one-arm supported row, related to the recurring primary row and prior bilateral explosive rows. Independent arm force is the job; not counted as new simply because the implement changes.
explosive.key: One-Arm Row — supported dumbbell speed pull

explosive.name: Floor Press — single-arm light dumbbell speed press
explosive.job: Accelerate an independent pressing load while the trunk resists rolling.
explosive.cue: Supine, feet fixed and free arm resting on floor; upper arm touches gently, then press quickly without releasing the dumbbell; lower 2 s.
explosive.replacement: a self-anchored single-arm band speed press with the nonworking hand securing the tail if floor/load handling is unsuitable
explosive.identity: Floor Press family; single-arm rapid execution proposed
explosive.uniqueness_reason: Adds an asymmetric load-control problem to Class 4 bilateral speed pressing. It remains a floor-press variant; six light reps are separate from the later challenging unilateral strength sets.
explosive.key: Floor Press — single-arm light dumbbell speed press

explosive.name: Band Lat Pulldown — single-arm rapid elbow drive
explosive.job: Keep independent overhead pulling with the ribs held level.
explosive.cue: Rated overhead attachment, tall kneeling base; quick elbow-to-rib draw, controlled 2 s return, no side bend.
explosive.replacement: a single-arm supported dumbbell speed row if no suitable overhead anchor exists; record the vertical-pull gap
explosive.identity: band-lat-pulldown parent; same single-arm execution as Class 3
explosive.uniqueness_reason: Explicit Class 3 repeat at two rather than three reps per arm. A new one-arm hanging task would raise support demands; the externally resisted pull is retained beside the new receive-to-one-arm task.
explosive.key: Band Lat Pulldown — single-arm rapid elbow drive

explosive.name: Landmine Push Press — single arm, shallow dip
explosive.job: Coordinate a small shared leg preload into one arm's forward/upward drive without turning.
explosive.cue: Feet stay fixed, short knee dip; extend legs then finish with one arm. Keep sleeve in hand, lower 2 s; no jump or re-bend catch.
explosive.replacement: the strict single-arm speed press if dip-to-arm timing or torso control is not demonstrated; use band pressing if bar fit fails
explosive.identity: landmine explosive-press family; unilateral non-flight delivery proposed
explosive.uniqueness_reason: Extends Class 5 bilateral force-transfer task to one arm with an anti-rotation demand. Not a new family; two repetitions per arm prevent a second major pressing workload.
explosive.key: Landmine Push Press — single arm, shallow dip

explosive.name: Medicine Ball Chest Pass — stationary, paused
explosive.job: Finish with two symmetric releases to check that the athlete can reconnect both arms to the same forward line.
explosive.cue: Fixed parallel feet, still 1 s chest hold, simultaneous release without dip or twist.
explosive.replacement: a self-anchored bilateral band speed press if containment is unsuitable
explosive.uniqueness_reason: Explicit Class 1 repeat for a tiny bilateral integration dose. A new overhead or moving throw was rejected because it adds an unrelated position/step after the side-specific work. It is not an extra comparison test.
explosive.key: Medicine Ball Chest Pass — stationary, paused

resilience.name: Supine Dumbbell Serratus Reach — single arm, light
resilience.job: Control shoulder-blade reach without trunk roll under a small unilateral load.
resilience.cue: Very light dumbbell over shoulder; elbow straight, reach 2 s, hold 1 s, lower 2 s; keep ribs level.
resilience.replacement: an unloaded single-arm supine reach if the lightest implement causes rotation
resilience.identity: Proposed exact execution; no verified canonical identifier
resilience.key: Supine Dumbbell Serratus Reach — single arm, light

resilience.name: Bilateral Band External Rotation — elbows at sides
resilience.job: Light shoulder-rotator strengthening to control upper-arm position during the day's press and pull.
resilience.cue: Unanchored band between hands, elbows at ribs; rotate outward 2 s, hold 1 s, return 2 s without shrugging.
resilience.replacement: a lower-tension band and shorter comfortable range
resilience.key: Bilateral Band External Rotation — elbows at sides

primary.name: Floor Press — one dumbbell, single arm
primary.job: Main unilateral pressing strength while resisting trunk roll.
primary.cue: Free arm rests on floor for balance without pushing; keep feet down. Lower 2 s, gentle floor pause 1 s, press decisively without rotating.
primary.replacement: a lighter floor press through controlled comfortable range

primary.name: One-Arm Row — dumbbell, hand and knee on bench
primary.job: Load the arm-driven backward draw while support prevents torso rotation.
primary.cue: Draw elbow toward hip, hold 1 s, lower 2 s; stop before the shoulder rolls forward or the trunk turns.
primary.replacement: a thigh-supported dumbbell row with the same arm path if a bench does not fit

primary.name: Landmine Press — strict single arm
primary.job: Load the independent forward/upward arm drive with a stable torso.
primary.cue: Feet fixed, bar at shoulder; no dip, press under control, lower 2 s without side bend or rib flare.
primary.replacement: a single-arm self-anchored band chest press if the minimum bar load or grip is unsuitable

primary.name: Dumbbell Rear-Delt Row — bilateral, hinged
primary.job: Strengthen the wider-elbow backward draw that controls the arm-open position.
primary.cue: Hold a still hinge; elbows about 60 degrees from torso, pull to upper ribs, hold 1 s, lower 2 s.
primary.replacement: a chest-supported version only on an inspected bench with adequate arm clearance

primary.name: Dumbbell Skull Crusher — floor-supported
primary.job: Load elbow extension for the finish of a forceful press.
primary.cue: Neutral grips, upper arms near vertical; lower 2 s beside the ears, extend under control without shoulder swing.
primary.replacement: a lighter floor-supported elbow extension through comfortable range

primary.name: Dumbbell Hammer Curl — simultaneous arms
primary.job: Load elbow flexors for finishing the backward draw without another shoulder-extension set.
primary.cue: Upper arms stay at ribs; lift 1 s, hold 1 s, lower 2 s, without hip swing or wrist collapse.
primary.replacement: a lighter neutral-grip curl without body movement

progression: Class 6 used one set of six for each primary lift. Here the main press changes to single-arm Floor Press 2 × 5 per arm, with one set of each supporting lift, including Row 1 × 6 per arm and strict Landmine Press 1 × 6 per arm. Seven rounds expand to eleven actual bouts because three lifts are unilateral; 64 task reps must not be mistaken for 64 bilateral cycles. No automatic load escalation: choose loads afresh for unilateral control, and retain a one-set version if readiness does not support the second press set. Before future advancement require both sides to demonstrate the stated control/reserve and reported recovery.
audit_findings: No single-arm hand-flight push-ups or one-hand ball catches were added. Six gentle bilateral catches and eight total throws are counted. Unilateral strength and speed reps include both arms; reduced supporting press/curl reps offset extra unilateral bouts. One new coordination task, three related variants and two specified repeats are disclosed. Stabilization remains light and specifically resists unilateral trunk roll.
next_job: Class 8 should refine pulling through a useful range and force transfer to the hands, reviewing the extra unilateral bouts and grip/elbow response before any increase.
